analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.

analysis_refs.heading: Owner updates and additional-source delivery
analysis_refs.text:
The owner postponed Redis and confirmed that Codex owns children’s sourcing. The
existing OpenAlex key was rechecked and accepted; no replacement key or owner
curation is pending. Free source login is explicitly allowed. The API distinguishes
`free_account_required` from anonymous full text and unknown-price registration;
ordinary book search includes the reviewed set when its flag is enabled.

analysis_refs.heading: Implemented and checked locally
analysis_refs.text:
- Redis coordinator, shared record/page caches, stored federation sessions,
  application-wide source counters and their setup/CI prerequisites are removed.
- One live source request per search/detail. Native cursors are signed, bounded,
  context-bound and usable after process restart. Replay makes another request.
- Deterministic tests cover source routing, no fan-out, token tampering/expiry,
  old-session rejection, page cycles/depth, underfilled pages, access classes,
  invalid provider responses, provider errors, cancellation and exact resolution.
- OpenAlex verifies free allowance/known pricing/zero prepaid funds before each
  request. Existing tests reject paid balances, changed prices and exhaustion.
- 570 server tests pass with zero skips; 179 client tests and typecheck pass.
  The disposable PostgreSQL used for existing account regression tests is local
  test infrastructure, not a free-content runtime dependency or hosted resource.
- 62 focused desktop/mobile browser checks pass, including live coverage,
  paging, source switching/website links, reading, save/reload/reopen and three
  reading lights. Full build, isolated client-only build, SEO/deployment checks,
  12 Python importer tests and refresh-script tests pass.

analysis_refs.heading: Actual sources and browser
analysis_refs.text:
[Direct source probes](evidence/2026-11-03/direct-live-probes.json) use official
APIs and the existing OpenAlex key, without store bindings. Mathematics selects
OpenAlex; malaria selects Europe PMC. Both return current readable metadata,
resolve exact native records live and continue to another page. A Europe PMC
continuation overlapped one record, confirming why live paging is not a frozen,
globally duplicate-free snapshot. The browser removes repeated source keys.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
The existing OpenAlex key was rechecked on 2026-11-01: the API accepted it and
its free budget/search-price/no-prepaid conditions passed. No replacement key is
requested. The owner postponed Redis setup; live paper dispatch stays off until
hosted coordination is configured, independently of the local book catalogs.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
Other source daily budgets allow 1–100,000, minute budgets 1–300; these are
configuration bounds, not recommended traffic allowances. Choose lower team
limits deliberately. OpenAlex also needs the server-only `OPENALEX_API_KEY`.
Its rate-limit endpoint is checked before each uncached request; unknown pricing,
a paid allowance/prepaid balance, missing metadata or exhausted free funds block
dispatch. Local limits are conservative; other uses of the same key still draw
on the provider's allowance. No paid usage is enabled by this code.

analysis_refs.heading: Free-content production release
analysis_refs.text:
**Current revision (2026-11-03):** the owner authorized the
[simple free live plan](SIMPLE_LIVE_PLAN.md), #156. Release/hosted verification is
tracked in #159. Europe PMC/OpenAlex can run directly with no data store; the
blanket Redis gate is superseded. This release must retain verified free-budget
guards and existing account settings. The November 1 evidence below records the
initial book release, rather than the current paper prerequisites.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Engineering design
analysis_refs.text:
One supported adapter is called per request, with bounded deadlines/response
sizes and no automatic retry/fan-out. OpenAlex also checks its free allowance
before its search or exact-record request. Client disconnects cancel work.

analysis_refs.heading: Cost and limits
analysis_refs.text:
Europe PMC uses its public API. OpenAlex uses the existing server-only key;
verify its free allowance, accepted endpoint pricing and zero prepaid balance
before dispatch. Exhaustion, paid balances or unknown policy stop the request.
No paid fallback or paid infrastructure is introduced. Normal hosting usage
continues under the existing Vercel plan; future hosting costs are not guaranteed
to be zero.

analysis_refs.heading: Configuration and delivery
analysis_refs.text:
Keep the existing discovery flag and strong cursor signer. Enable Europe PMC
and optionally OpenAlex with its key. Remove Redis and per-source application
daily/minute budget variables from active setup. No client-exposed credentials
or database migration.

analysis_refs.heading: Multi-source papers follow-up
analysis_refs.text:
DOAJ, arXiv and OpenAlex now have bounded adapters, source-native identities and
per-location access/licence handling. Fresh [policy observations](evidence/2026-11-01/source-policies.json)
verify DOAJ's 2 RPS and arXiv's 3-second/single-connection aggregate rules. The
configured OpenAlex key reported $1/day free allowance, $0.001 ordinary search
and zero prepaid funds; runtime rechecks those conditions before dispatch.
Operational limits and caveats are in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md).

analysis_refs.heading: Free source accounts and additional source delivery
analysis_refs.text:
Current real-source records: 1,000 Gutenberg, 1,909 textbook, 30 Book Dash and
three reviewed StoryWeaver records. This is 2,942 bounded metadata records,
not a worldwide catalog size or a search-match total. Eight sources have
implementations: these four book sources plus four existing live paper adapters.
The OpenAlex key was rechecked successfully. Redis remains deferred by the owner;
no hosted store, source account or production enablement was created here.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage
analysis_refs.text:
- Provider contracts: valid/empty/malformed response, missing fields, absent license, preview/borrow/embargo, stale links, 429/503 and schema drift.
- Identity: same DOI across indexes, preprint vs publication, arXiv versions, translations, chapter vs book, missing ISBN, unrelated same title, Zenodo concept vs version DOI.
- Search: partial/all-source failure, exhausted budget, unsupported filters, cancellation, no skipped/duplicate pages, expired cursor, honest totals.
- Imports: interrupted/repeated OAI page, tombstone, expired token, corrupt/empty bulk file and rollback.
- End-to-end: title/author/DOI, free filters, details, external HTML/reader/PDF/EPUB where offered, browser back, unchanged ISBN/library/shelf flows; launch-country checks beyond server-region behavior.
- Capacity: uncached searches/day and peak concurrency. At the observed OpenAlex price, ordinary search cost is uncached calls × $0.001; paging/enrichment add requests. arXiv 1/3 sec is at most 20/min before contention. Configure degradation before enabling traffic.

analysis_refs.heading: 9. Inputs still needed for implementation
analysis_refs.text: Verify the configured OpenAlex key with an actual authenticated request and select a real application contact email. Decide expected traffic and commercial/noncommercial use before setting quotas and eligibility. Choose initial children's languages/levels and launch countries before feeds and access validation. No missing input blocks this research or its publication; the proposal itself authorizes no new paid resources or accounts.

analysis_refs.heading: C03 — Published research articles
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval strategy.** Test existing OpenAlex coverage first, using a known work
and its actual host attribution. Current [OpenAlex search documentation](https://help.openalex.org/api/searching/)
describes work text/keyword search and separate entity searches; an institution
name match does not establish that its repository holds the paper. Use the
documented filters and inspect individual locations. Preserve the existing free
allowance guard. A new publisher API or permitted OAI/export import is justified
when the index demonstrably misses useful holdings. An OJS website or a DOI
registration record alone does not prove reusable full-item discovery.

analysis_refs.heading: Handoff and research limits
analysis_refs.text:
This review inspected official directory/protocol documentation, not production
API behavior, source-login access or complete catalogs. The old OpenAlex docs URL
failed after redirect; the linked Help Center route worked. RePEc's root page
returned a gateway error while its archive/policy pages worked. These are tooling
observations, not evidence of source-wide downtime. Current prices, permission,
freshness and per-origin free access still require qualification before enablement.

analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. analysis_refs.heading: Credentials and implementation inputs
analysis_refs.text:
1. Verify **`OPENALEX_API_KEY`** in the backend. The replacement environment reports the variable configured; no authenticated OpenAlex request was made during this repository transfer. At the research date the free account included $1/day of API usage, roughly 1,000 ordinary search requests before caching. Disable paid overages unless deliberately budgeted.
2. Choose a real **application contact email** for request identification and, if enabled, Unpaywall's required `email` parameter. No email was invented, registered, or sent during this work.

analysis_refs.heading: Contracts and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- One provider per server request; the browser coordinates the search. No Redis,
  SQL, hosted cache, persisted session or new account/service.
- Fixed-origin adapters bound response size, deadline and paging. Signed cursors
  bind provider, query, types, language, page size and expiry; they work across
  function restarts without storing query results. Changed indexes can change
  pages; exact-key deduplication never merges similar titles or distinct editions.
- The new transport serializes requests per host within an instance, spaces them
  two seconds apart and honors 429 Retry-After. It has no automatic retries.
  This courtesy is not a global request quota across Vercel instances.
- Python's official compressed symbol inventory is bounded and cached for one
  hour in process memory. Search is over symbol/section names, not arbitrary
  full documentation text. Version and same-origin URL checks fail closed.
- GDL uses its public content-search route and published WordPress REST book-ID
  route for exact details. Word-level metadata checks reject substring noise
  such as `Rain` matching only `Shakrain`. Its provider offset advances even when
  inspected rows fail relevance, so filtering does not trap pagination.
- Thoth searches active monographs/edited books in explicit publisher IDs. Exact
  resolution verifies publisher membership and active status. Only canonical
  digital links on reviewed publisher hosts become reading/download actions;
  print, retail and unreviewed mirrors do not.
- LoC requires `access_restricted=false`, digitization and an online resource for
  free access. BHL searches only its biodiversity collection and excludes known
  access-restricted items. Their content rights still vary by item.
- LibriVox is title search and distinct recording identity. Its documented JSON
  404 for no audiobooks is an empty result; other errors remain failures. US
  public-domain statements do not claim worldwide rights.
- Snapshot sources remain labelled incomplete/stale when appropriate. Unknown
  access is hidden by default; an explicit checkbox reveals labelled results with a source record link; no old
  observation is refreshed merely because a user searches it.
- Existing OpenAlex free-allowance and zero-paid-balance checks remain unchanged.
  No key is returned to the browser. No full books/audio are copied.
